reason: The tile needs a secure cradle for the tethered test, so I’ll assemble those parts first.
expectation: I expect the tile to fit into the cradle, ready to be mounted in the test stand.

alternatives.reason: The safety tether is important too, but I’ll prepare the tile first.

effect: The tile is cradled; I still need to prepare the stand and power.
reason: The tether should help keep the lift test contained.
expectation: I expect the safety tether to attach to the test-stand base.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the switched power supply also seems useful, but I want the restraint in place first.

effect: The base now has its safety tether; the guide posts can be fitted next.
reason: The guide posts should keep the tile's movement aligned during the test.
expectation: I expect the posts to attach to the tethered base, ready to guide the cradled tile.

alternatives.reason: The switched battery supply is also needed, but I’ll finish preparing the stand first.

effect: The stand now has guides, so the cradled tile can be fitted.
reaction: Straightforward progress toward a contained test.
reason: I’ll fit the tile into the prepared stand before connecting power.
expectation: I expect the cradled tile to mount inside the guided stand, with the tether keeping it contained.

alternatives.reason: The switched power supply is also needed, but I prefer to secure the tile first.

effect: The cradled tile is now in the test stand; the switched power supply remains to be prepared.
reason: The switch and battery are the only offered combination, and the tile needs power for its test.
expectation: I expect a battery supply with a spring-return switch that can power the tile during testing.

effect: The hold-to-lift supply is ready to connect to the tile in its stand.
reaction: The spring-return control makes the test feel more contained.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the tile needs its supply for testing.
expectation: I expect the supply to connect to the tile, allowing it to lift while the switch is held.

effect: The powered tile rises until the tether stops it and settles when released; the remaining question is how it handles a load.
reaction: The sudden propeller-free lift is surprising, even though the tile’s invented ability was stated upfront.
reason: The test weight is the only offered combination and should help establish what the tile can lift.
expectation: I expect the weight to be attached for a controlled lift test, though I don’t know whether the tile can raise it.

effect: The tile lifted the test weight more slowly, completing the contained test and showing that the added load affects its rise.
reaction: Seeing the invented lift respond to a load made the test more interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the weight was most worthwhile: it gave the fantasy mechanism a concrete behavior to observe.

leastWorthwhile.text: The early assembly was straightforward but repetitive, with little feedback beyond the names of the parts created.

surprise.text: The tile rose without a propeller or balloon, although its invented ability had been announced beforehand.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless; the cradle, guides, tether and switch all seemed relevant to a controlled test.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the lift tile is used in the fair, though I hope the next chapter offers more meaningful choices than this mostly linear setup.
